title: International Business Machines (IBM) Q3 Earnings Beat Estimates as Software Revenue Jumps 8%
excerpt: Revenue of $17.1 billion and operating EPS of $2.95 both topped consensus; IBM raised its full-year free cash flow outlook.
body:
• IBM's third-quarter revenue rose 5% to $17.1 billion (6% at constant currency), beating the $16.87 billion consensus; operating EPS of $2.95 topped the $2.88 estimate.
  • Software revenue grew 8% to $7.8 billion, led by Red Hat hybrid cloud (up 11%) and data (up 19%); consulting was flat at $5.3 billion and infrastructure rose 4% to $3.7 billion.
  • GAAP EPS rose 26% to $2.31 and quarterly free cash flow reached $3.0 billion.
  • IBM raised its full-year free cash flow outlook to growth of more than $1 billion year over year and kept its 4–5% constant-currency revenue growth guide.

International Business Machines (IBM) reported third-quarter results after the market closed on Wednesday that beat expectations on both revenue and earnings, as its software and infrastructure businesses accelerated and consulting stabilised. The shares rose about 4.5% in after-hours trading.

Revenue for the quarter ended September 30 rose 5% year over year to $17.1 billion — 6% at constant currency — ahead of the $16.87 billion consensus estimate compiled by Zacks. Operating (non-GAAP) diluted EPS increased 11% to $2.95, beating the $2.88 estimate, while GAAP diluted EPS from continuing operations rose 26% to $2.31. Operating pre-tax margin expanded 70 basis points to 19.3%, and free cash flow for the quarter was $3.0 billion, taking the year-to-date figure to $7.8 billion.

Software Leads, Consulting Flat

Software was the growth engine, with revenue up 8% to $7.8 billion. Within it, Hybrid Cloud (Red Hat) rose 11%, Data jumped 19% and Transaction Processing grew 9%, partly offset by a 3% decline in Automation. Consulting revenue was flat at $5.3 billion, up 2% at constant currency, as strength in Strategy and Technology offset a 2% decline in Intelligent Operations. Infrastructure revenue rose 4% to $3.7 billion: distributed infrastructure surged 31% and hybrid infrastructure grew 8%, while IBM Z mainframe revenue fell 20% against a strong product-cycle comparison. Financing revenue slipped 4% to $192 million.

"For the full year, we continue to expect constant currency revenue growth in the range of four-to-five percent, and we now expect free cash flow to increase by more than $1 billion year-over-year."

— Arvind Krishna, IBM Chairman and CEO

Cash Flow Outlook Raised

The company kept its full-year constant-currency revenue growth guide at 4–5% but raised its free cash flow outlook, now expecting growth of more than $1 billion over 2025. IBM's GAAP gross margin eased 50 basis points to 56.8%, while the operating gross margin was 58.5%. The board declared a quarterly cash dividend of $1.69 per share, extending a run of consecutive quarterly dividends paid every year since 1916.

For Indian-American investors and the large number of Indian-origin professionals in IBM's US workforce, the quarter's message is that the company's AI-and-hybrid-cloud pivot continues to be carried by software: Red Hat and data services are where the growth — and the hiring demand for cloud and AI skills — is concentrated, while the traditional mainframe cycle cools.

Cash Generation and the AI Angle

Cash generation strengthened through the year: net cash from operating activities reached $11.8 billion for the first nine months, with free cash flow of $7.8 billion. CFO James Kavanaugh credited "strong operational execution" and the company's internal productivity programme, which IBM says is funding continued investment while supporting the dividend. Management framed client demand around deploying AI across whole operating models rather than narrow pilots — the shift it calls "Super Intelligence" in client work — with cybersecurity a notable driver inside consulting as companies worry about securing agentic AI systems.

What to watch next is whether consulting, flat this quarter, returns to growth in the fourth quarter, and whether the IBM Z decline moderates as the mainframe cycle normalises. The full-year guide — constant-currency revenue growth of 4–5% and free cash flow up more than $1 billion — leaves the burden of proof on a seasonally strong final quarter.
